races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Bahrain Turf Club Desmond Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up specialist for O'Meara and Keane who has been struggling for form (three zeros in recent runs), returning over a mile after a string of 7f efforts — the step back up in trip helps but the absence of a recent win and weak recent form make this a tough ask in Group 3 company.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this 5-year-old hold-up type who has placed four times in similar company on comparable ground but lacks the finishing kick to convert; 40 days off and a record of 1W from 13 similar-going runs sums up the limitation.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan rides this Joseph O'Brien 4-year-old who recorded a career-best win over 7f on Good ground last time and is lightly weighted for a race of this class; his natural instinct is to race at the rear, and in a field already loaded with hold-up types he will need a clear run late — the style fit discount is real here.

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: McAteer takes the mount on this Marnane-trained 5-year-old who boasts three wins over this exact trip on similar ground and sits comfortably in the prominent position that suits him; fresh off 39 days he has the profile to press the pace and last home.

runners_data.name: Celtic Motif
runners_data.note: The J P O'Brien runner who led and won over course and distance last time out, and Sheridan will look to exploit that experience by controlling the race from the front; the clash with Needle Match makes an uncontested lead unlikely, but Celtic Motif is the more battle-hardened of the two pace-setters.

runners_data.name: Al Haarith
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this classy 3-year-old who won his last start over course and distance and has strong claims at a 3lb age allowance advantage; racing prominently on fast ground at Leopardstown where he has already shown his quality, the profile is very strong.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides this A P O'Brien 3-year-old who is dropping back from 9f–12f trips, having won over 9f on Good ground; the shorter trip is the key question but Moore's positioning instinct on a strong-pace day could allow him to finish with real purpose through the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Needle Match
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand brings this William Haggas 3-year-old back from 96 days off, which is the standout concern in a Group 3 on fast ground; a confirmed front-runner who will duel for the lead with Celtic Motif, and if the Haggas preparation is spot-on he can be dangerous — but the lengthy absence makes confidence hard to justify.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Bolger's 3-year-old arrives on the back of three consecutive wins including back-to-back 10f–12f victories, now dropping sharply to a mile — the trip shortening is a genuine query even though the form figures are pristine and McDonogh is an astute navigator of a small field.

races.paceDynamic: Needle Match and Celtic Motif are the two confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field, and on Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown over a mile they will push each other into an honest, competitive gallop from the off rather than either stealing an uncontested lead. Al Haarith and Tokenomics will press close behind, meaning the tempo is unlikely to collapse, and the race is set to be run at a genuine clip throughout. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate in their natural positions — Cowardofthecounty is a genuine hold-up horse who will be further back than the midfield slot suggests, as the prominent berths are already contested by several others. With two pace-setters driving each other along and a fast surface, this race shape will suit prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel smoothly within the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sudden burst — hold-up horses that need a late collapse of the tempo are at a disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Needle Match and Celtic Motif set a genuine honest gallop and the race is run at even tempo throughout, rewarding those who travel well just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners post a solid fractions and begin to weaken entering the final two furlongs, leaving the race to those who tracked them comfortably in the prominent-to-midfield tier. Al Haarith, Isaac Newton and Tokenomics are best placed to capitalise, having conserved energy behind a true pace on a fast surface.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Celtic Motif or Needle Match shakes off the other before the home turn and dictates at a sustainable clip, stealing a march on the field.
scenarios.body: Celtic Motif, who has a recent course win over the distance and the backing of the O'Brien yard, is best positioned to press and then assert if Needle Match fades after duelling — a horse with a tactical lead entering the straight on fast ground can be very hard to catch. Needle Match carries a lengthy absence of 96 days but Haggas runners often return fit, and Tom Marquand can judge pace well enough to exploit any gap that opens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns unusually hot and the front rank folds abruptly in the final furlong, creating a window for a late finisher to mow them down.
scenarios.body: Isaac Newton, racing back from longer trips, has the profile to finish powerfully if the tempo has been truly brutal, and Chicago Critic has strong staying form in this grade on similar ground. Cowardofthecounty is a genuine hold-up type here but the redistribution note reflects the risk of being further back than ideal in a compact field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Anyone's Race
scenarios.trigger: If Needle Match and Celtic Motif nullify each other in a scrappy duel and the pace becomes uneven, turning the race into a chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A muddled tempo with surges and checks would open the race up to any horse with tactical speed and a clear passage, most likely one tracking in third or fourth rather than either end of the field. Sparan Nua, lightly raced and in excellent recent form over shorter trips stepping up, and Tokenomics both have the positional speed to profit if the shape of the race becomes unpredictable.

watchPoints.text: Al Haarith holds a deeply compelling profile — course-and-distance winner, 3lb age allowance, strong jockey booking, and a pace scenario that sets up perfectly for a prominent racer to pounce; if he travels smoothly in second or third he is the most dangerous horse in the race.

Needle Match's 96-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — watch for him in the parade ring and early in the race; if he jumps cleanly and settles into a rhythm he could dictate, but if he shows any rustiness in the duel with Celtic Motif the front-running plan unravels quickly.

Sparan Nua's drop from 10f–12f to a mile on fast ground is a genuine concern — watch how sharply McDonogh sends him into the race; if he needs to be ridden for pace rather than allowed to stride, the trip is likely too short for his current profile.

The Joseph O'Brien yard saddles three runners (Celtic Motif, Cowardofthecounty, Al Haarith) — with a 13/72 14-day record, monitor market moves for yard confidence, and note that Al Haarith carries the lightest weight and the most compelling form of the three.

Isaac Newton's move from 9f–12f trips back to a mile is worth tracking in running — if Ryan Moore settles him close to the pace rather than holding up from the rear, it signals the stable believes the trip is fine and his chance should be taken more seriously.

races.name: Ballyroan Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: De Bromhead-trained seven-year-old with genuine form at this trip (placed over 14f on good), but naturally a prominent racer who is pushed into midfield here by the volume of pace in this field — his chance is shape-dependent and he needs things to go wrong ahead of him.|

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will go straight to the lead; OR 100, five-year-old with good recent place form at this trip and on this going, though his Flat win record is limited — his role is pace-setter and he will determine how hot this race gets.|

runners_data.name: Ethical Diamond
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 118 with Ryan Moore booked, three wins on good or faster ground in recent history and progressive form at 12-14f; the 1m4f trip looks manageable given his 12f win record and the step up in distance is the only query.|

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained seven-year-old who has won twice on Stanmore (AW) but turf form on good shows a mixed record; prominent runner who will want to be in the firing line early and the return to 1m4f turf from shorter trips is a slight query.|

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Harrington's four-year-old has strong good-ground form and three wins in recent form, though all recent wins came at shorter than today's 1m4f; 74 days off is the most notable layoff in the field and the step to Group 3 company over an unproven trip requires a leap of faith.|

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up performer who is the only genuine closer in the field; Colin Keane booked, won last time over 12f on soft and placed over 16f on good — the fast ground here is fine, and his late-run style becomes more potent if the pace is strong.|

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: O'Brien four-year-old whose natural instinct is to race prominently, though the congestion here pushes him into a midfield position he is unlikely to relish; recent form over shorter trips (8-10f) is a concern at 1m4f and he races at a discount in any shape requiring him to hold up.|

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Three-year-old co-pacemaker alongside Dallas Star, trained by J P Murtagh; has placed at Group level and won over 10f, so the 1m4f is an open question stamina-wise — will set the early gallop but the younger, lighter weight (125lbs) could see him crack before the business end.|

runners_data.name: Endorsement
runners_data.note: DBM rides this O'Brien three-year-old who has placed five times in recent outings including two second-place finishes; a naturally prominent or just-off-the-pace type who is well-placed in terms of form trajectory, though the step from 10-12f to 1m4f is unproven.|

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star and Asakir are both confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m4f — this is not a false-pace scenario. Four of the nine runners want prominent positions, meaning Green Impact, Gaucher, and Ethical Diamond will be jostling for the front rank through the early stages, compressing the midfield and creating meaningful traffic pressure two to three furlongs out. Omni Man and Ascending are both naturally prominent types who are displaced into midfield by this congestion, meaning they will not be racing in their preferred role and their chances are shape-dependent as a result. This race shape — honest gallop, compressed midfield, genuine test of stamina on fast ground — heavily favours a high-class, prominent-to-midfield horse that can travel within the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp sprint, which points directly to those with the strongest staying form and the biggest class margin.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Asakir push each other through a genuine gallop and the race is run to suit a high-class horse tracking the pace.
scenarios.body: The honest fractions will string the field out early and create a stamina test that rewards the highest-rated, best-actioned horse within touching distance of the pace; the congested prominent group will thin out naturally under pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Late Swooper
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out and the pace is genuinely excessive, leaving the race wide open for a hold-up horse to pounce.
scenarios.body: Layfayette, who has shown strong recent form winning over 12f and placing over 16f, is ideally positioned in a hold-up role and Colin Keane will be able to pick his way through a tiring field; the fast ground suits his recent form profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Causes Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the four-horse battle for prominent positions creates significant interference and traffic issues between the 3f and 2f poles, disrupting the race for those caught in the squeeze.
scenarios.body: Horses that have secured their position cleanly early — particularly the two confirmed front-runners who bypass the traffic — will benefit, as will any horse wide enough to avoid the congestion; Ethical Diamond with Ryan Moore is likely to be positioned shrewdly around the trouble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly steady early, compressing the field and turning the race into a sprint finish from 2f out that favours those shuffled back.
scenarios.body: Ascending and Omni Man, both naturally prominent horses racing out of their preferred role in the midfield, would have the tactical speed to benefit from a falsely-run race — though both carry the caveat that this is not their natural shape and their style-fit discount applies.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star and Asakir could set a punishing early gallop — watch for either runner cracking inside the final 3f, which would dramatically reshape the race for those tracking just off the pace like Ethical Diamond and Gaucher.

The four-runner battle for prominent positions (Ethical Diamond, Gaucher, Green Impact, plus the front-runners) risks serious crowding and bumping between the 6f and 4f marks — horses drawn wide or ridden patiently by experienced jockeys will have the clearest passage.
Green Impact's 74-day layoff is the longest in the field and Shane Foley will need to manage her carefully early; watch for any signs of rustiness if she over-races chasing the pace.

Layfayette at age nine is the only true hold-up horse in the race — watch Colin Keane for how aggressively he challenges once the pace collapses in the straight, as this is his only realistic winning shape.

Ascending and Omni Man are both naturally prominent horses mapped into midfield by the pace volume — watch whether either jockey attempts to push forward early despite the congestion, which would be a tell that connections believe the race pace will be insufficient.

races.name: Carnival de Leop Handicap

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3) partners this hold-up specialist for Michael Mulvany; 15 days since a run over 8f on Good is ideal freshness, and with strong similar-going form (2 wins, 6 places in 15 starts), he needs the pace to be honest enough to close into — in a controlled-tempo race he will be playing catch-up from deep.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Alan Persse (5) partners this six-year-old for Patrick J Flynn; a chronic hold-up runner with zero wins or places in his last five starts, all on Good or Standard, and his recent 15th and 13th finishes in similar fields suggest he is operating below the level needed to get competitive here regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Pete's Dream
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and the pivotal horse in this race shape; Andrew Slattery's four-year-old won over 8f on Good and faces no pace rival to challenge him early, meaning he can control fractions entirely — STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) signals he is operating as a confirmed leader today, which is actually his ideal scenario here rather than a concern, though the handicapper has him on a fair mark.

runners_data.name: Wellwhatshappenin
runners_data.note: Tagged as a hold-up runner who fades in the finish; 139 days off the track is a significant concern for Eddie and Patrick Harty's four-year-old, and though she has won and placed over 7f at Dundalk on Standard ground, Good to Firm at Leopardstown on a long absence asks significant questions — Jamie Powell faces an uphill task.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns (5) rides this consistent hold-up type for R P Burns; has a placed effort at 7f on Good in recent form and genuine closing ability, though 12 days since last run and an eight-year-old's reliance on a strong pace means a slow early tempo works against his chance of getting involved.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old for R Donohoe fitted with a tongue-bar; prominent racer who has shown consistent form around this trip on Good and Good to Firm surfaces with multiple placed efforts over 7-8f, and Sam Coen (5) can tuck in behind Pete's Dream at minimal cost — no obvious going concern and only 12 days since last run keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this hold-up type for Peter Fahey; 246 days off the course is an extreme layoff for an eight-year-old, all recent form is at 6f on Standard or Heavier ground, and stepping up to 7f on Good to Firm represents two unknowns at once — hard to include with confidence.

runners_data.name: Launch Time
runners_data.note: Cian Hughes's four-year-old wears a visor and has solid good-ground form; Colin Keane is a major positive here and the horse's style — prominent, travelling well through a race — is perfectly suited to tracking an uncontested leader, though he has been stepping up in trip from his 8f wins and 7f may catch him slightly short.

runners_data.name: Dress Dance
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's four-year-old wears a tongue-piece and is flagged as fading in the finish; a genuine hold-up runner whose natural role has been redistributed forward by the crowded rear of this field, meaning Siobhan Rutledge will have to manage a horse that is out of its comfort zone positionally — 79 days off and poor recent form over 10f confirm this is a long-shot proposition.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Donal Kinsella's four-year-old wears a tongue-piece and hood; has a win and a second on Good ground over 8f showing ability, but as a true hold-up type mapped forward because of the overcrowded rear, Robbie Colgan will find it difficult to recreate the conditions that brought out his best — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) underlines the positional squeeze he faces.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: T G McCourt's four-year-old wears a pom-pom and has run exclusively over 5-6f in recent starts, making this 7f trip a clear extension; Sadhbh Tormey (7) is apprentice-claimed but the horse's entire form profile is built around shorter-trip finishing bursts, and being redistributed out of its natural hold-up berth compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Cordouan
runners_data.note: Patrick McGettigan (5) rides this veteran hold-up type for P Sweeney; flagged as fading in the finish and mapped forward out of its natural rear position, with 21 days since a midfield effort and a history of 8th-25th finishes in recent starts — no compelling reason to expect improvement from a positional switch that is essentially involuntary.

runners_data.name: Mogwli
runners_data.note: W McCreery's nine-year-old wears a visor; 86 days off the track and five consecutive finishing positions of 0-0-0-0-0 since returning from a previous break paint a bleak picture, and as a hold-up horse bumped to midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.93), Megan Telford-Kelly (7) faces a formidable task to find any competitive thread.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: J G Coogan's four-year-old has only four career runs, all on Good or Standard, with a best of 6th; recent form figures of 9-7-6 show no progression, and as a hold-up type whose race position is effectively determined by the overcrowded rear rather than by choice, Scott McCullagh will be working against the shape.

runners_data.name: Smaoineamh Sile
runners_data.note: Robert Whearty rides this eight-year-old for Conor David Maxwell; wears a tongue-piece, flagged as fading, and has not finished in the first nine in any of her last five starts — the 21-day turnaround is fine but the horse's deeper form profile and positional redistribution mean she is one of the least likely beneficiaries of any outcome.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Ben Coen aboard for S M Duffy; 94 days off and five consecutive finishing positions of 0-0-0-0-0 confirm this four-year-old wearing a pom-pom is badly out of form, and a fade-in-finish flag combined with genuine hold-up needs mapped forward into midfield leaves very little to work with.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes the mount for T J O'Mara; wears a hood and the fade flag applies — a hold-up horse whose 22-day return follows a 4th on Good over 8f, showing he retains some ability, but dropping to 7f on Good to Firm while being positionally squeezed out of his preferred late-running spot reduces his chance materially.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Terry Casey (7) rides for Joseph Anthony Murray; tongue-bar fitted, with trainer in form at 1/5 over 14 days — genuine recent positives, including a 3rd over 10f on Good, though the horse's hold-up profile being pushed into midfield by redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.92) and a step down in trip from 10f to 7f create real tactical problems.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: T G McCourt's five-year-old wears a pom-pom; has placed twice at 8f on Standard and showed some consistency in 2-3 finishes at Dundalk, and with a prominent style that is genuinely suited to sitting in the slipstream of Pete's Dream, this is one of the more credible threats — though the absence of a jockey name at declaration is a concern until confirmed.

runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and ran just three days ago — an extremely

races.paceDynamic: Pete's Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — with so many true hold-up types crowding the rear, the early tempo is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than furious. On Good to Firm ground over 7f at Leopardstown, a lone leader dictating from the front without being harassed creates a classic rails-save, run-your-own-race scenario that strongly advantages those who can sit just off the pace in the prominent or handy positions rather than those forced wide or trapped deep. Brains, Launch Time and Desert Of The Sea are the horses best positioned to track Pete's Dream through the race without burning energy, while Dinamine and The Blue Panther lurk as the most credible hold-up threats if they can find clear daylight in time. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Micasso, Dress Dance, Jazzit, Cordouan, Smaoineamh Sile and Cannonball Queen are all genuine closers who will find themselves shuffled into midfield in reality, and it is Pete's Dream, Brains and Launch Time who are most likely to actually secure their natural race positions. This race shape decisively favours horses racing prominently in the slipstream of an uncontested leader on quick ground — hold-up horses face a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream is allowed to stride into a clear early lead and the pace remains honest but controlled, setting a rhythm no rival can easily disrupt.
scenarios.body: Pete's Dream dictates every fraction from the front without harassment, conserving enough energy on Good to Firm ground to sustain his effort through the final furlong; prominent-handy trackers who can sit within a length or two are the ones with best chance of pegging him back or benefiting if he flattens. Brains and Launch Time in behind are the chief beneficiaries of a well-strung-out race run at a measured tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Pete's Dream sets a just-fast-enough gallop and the handy-prominent horses behind travel smoothly before asserting in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds in a single-file, controlled fashion and those sitting second or third without expending energy early — Brains, Launch Time — produce a sustained run from 2f out to overhaul the leader; the Good to Firm surface rewards those with a clean cruising speed rather than an explosive late burst. This is the shape that suits Colin Keane aboard Launch Time most, as the measured fractions allow him to time a challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to string out the field and one true closer can find a gap through the straight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With a 20-runner field even on a flat 7f track there can be traffic and a late-finishing hold-up horse benefits if runners fan wide in the straight; Dinamine and The Blue Panther, genuine closers with good-ground form, are best placed to exploit any pocket of light. However, this scenario is structurally undermined because so many nominal hold-up types will have been pushed forward involuntarily, meaning the finishing kick may arrive too late against a measured pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops an unexpectedly fast early tempo — perhaps through prominent types competing for position — causing Pete's Dream to overpace and collapse late.
scenarios.body: An unusually contested early pace could see the field bunch and then unravel in the final furlong, opening the door for a fresh-legged runner from further back; this is a low-probability shape given the clear lack of a rival front-runner to force the issue, but Jazzit or Micasso could benefit if the dynamics shift sharply. The redistribution of so many hold-up horses into midfield makes this scenario even harder to execute, as the theoretical closers are not actually in their optimal position.

races.name: Renault Ireland Handicap

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Dermot Weld who has placed at similar trips on Good ground before; OR 72 makes him one of the highest-rated in the field and he wants to be in the first four from the start to exploit a strong pace — 21 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs a truly run race over a trip where his stamina becomes an asset; trainer Seamus Fahey has had just one runner in the last fortnight and the big-field dynamics at Leopardstown make a clean run from the rear very difficult.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good ground over 8f for Willie McCreery and has placed repeatedly in similar conditions; hold-up in style but shorter than today's trip suits her finishing effort, and she has the sort of consistent form figures that make her competitive if she gets a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Quafftide
runners_data.note: Has run exclusively over 7f and 8f in recent starts so today's 9f on Good to Firm represents a step up in trip; hold-up style and no win on Good ground from four attempts makes this a speculative move into new territory.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare who has been running over longer trips (10f-13f) and is stepping back down in distance; her natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the crowded hold-up division — she is likely to be further forward than ideal, tempering her chance to deploy her finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on Good ground last time out for Paul Flynn and has a clear profile as a hold-up horse who needs a truly run race; the 9-day turnaround is quick but he is fit and his last win proves he is in form — if he can thread through, he is a live contender.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: Off 116 days and has been running over 8f on Soft or Heavy ground recently; the return from a long break combined with a step up to Good to Firm and an unexposed hold-up profile makes him unpredictable.

runners_data.name: Star Mind
runners_data.note: Placed on Good-ish ground over longer trips before and hold-up in style; Danny O'Leary (10) is a claim that softens the burden, but 83 days off and a big field means getting a clear run is not guaranteed — form figure of 1 over 9f on Soft is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Tequila
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Donagh O'Connor who has been placed on Good ground over 10f — today's 9f suits a horse who travels well enough to sit just behind the pace and produce a sustained run; no win from five Good-ground starts is the caveat.

runners_data.name: Ohmali
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over for Miss Natalia Lupini and the horse has hit the frame on Good ground before at 8f; a genuine hold-up type who is squeezed into a midfield position by the crowded rear contingent, making a finishing run harder to deliver than his profile suggests.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up performer who has been very consistent on Good ground over shorter trips — visor worn; his most recent win came over 8f on Flat so the step up to 9f is a question, and being channelled into midfield rather than the rear compromises how he wants to race.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Has run 3d ago which is a very quick turnaround; a hold-up type whose best form on Good ground came over shorter, and the blinkers suggest connections want more early energy — but being pushed into midfield against his natural instinct remains a structural concern.

runners_data.name: Jasmine Affanalis
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 8f on Good ground and her form figures show she goes well on this surface; a true hold-up horse who finds herself in midfield by necessity in this big field, meaning Luke McAteer will need to be very patient and hope for a clear lane late.

runners_data.name: Sonic Invader
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Noel Meade, whose T14 record of 4/23 shows the yard is firing; confirmed front-runner who has placed over much longer distances and now drops back sharply in trip — if he can get across and lead without a war, his stamina base could prove an asset late.

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up performer for Adrian McGuinness running in the tongue-plate; has placed in four of five starts on Good ground and the shorter trip relative to recent 10f-12f outings is interesting — one of the more likely horses to naturally settle near the rear given Adam Caffrey's quiet style.

runners_data.name: Ardeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form shows a string of poor finishes on Good ground; being mapped into midfield is an extra burden on top of disappointing recent numbers, and Patrick J Flynn's low T14 strike rate gives little support.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran hold-up performer who won over 8f on Heavy in a lower grade; Patrick McGettigan (5) riding, and a 21-day break is normal — but the horse has been struggling on Good ground in bigger fields and is squeezed into midfield by the crowded rear.

runners_data.name: Stepdance
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse for Henry de Bromhead whose most recent wins came over much longer trips (16f-17f); the compression down to 9f on Good to Firm is a significant drop in distance and the 69-day absence needs answering, but the yard is in excellent form (T14: 6/38).

runners_data.name: Little Wing
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a consistent profile over the last three starts on Good ground — all ninth or worse; Charles O'Brien has had just one runner in the last fortnight and the three-year-old has shown nothing yet to inspire confidence in a 25-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish across a run of 0s and poor finishes; prominent-style horse whose form in 10f-12f handicaps on Good ground has been uniformly poor, and the visor hasn't changed the pattern — hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Werifesteria
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Mrs John Harrington with Shane Foley aboard; three starts all at 12f on Good or Standard, so dropping to 9f should theoretically suit, but all three runs have been beaten — if she can dictate unaided she becomes dangerous, though Sonic Invader will not let that happen easily.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Ross O'Sullivan whose form on Good ground shows she has struggled in larger fields; Siobhan Rutledge rides, and being displaced into midfield by the congested hold-up division is an extra disadvantage to an already modest profile.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Prominent performer for Paul Flynn who has won twice on Good ground at around 9f — the most relevant recent form in the field; no jockey listed in the data but the trainer's T14 strike rate is active, the horse carries a hood and blinkers, and the recent form string of 013213 screams consistent performer at this level.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed five times in the last five runs on similar ground; ran just 8 days ago and the quick turnaround for an eight-year-old is worth noting — hood worn, and the big field holds structural risks for a horse who needs to come from off the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Werifesteria and Sonic Invader are the two confirmed front-runners in a field of 25, and with Colin Keane aboard the latter and Shane Foley on the former, both connections will want to use their pace assets from the gate — a genuine contest for the early lead is expected, meaning neither can simply coast in front and set a leisurely tempo. On Good to Firm ground at Leopardstown over 1m1f, a fast early pace between two duelling leaders will stretch the field and place a premium on horses travelling smoothly just off the pace without getting caught in traffic. Tachos, Tequila, Stepdance, and Nibras Rainbow are the most natural prominent-to-midfield horses who can exploit a strong gallop, while the large hold-up brigade will face the twin problems of traffic and needing a strong-enough finish to reel in anything that breaks clear. This race shape most favours the versatile prominent racer or a horse settled just off the pace in the first four or five — one who can track the speed without burning fuel early and produce a sustained run into the straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Guy's Girl, Wild Berries, Ohmali, Comfort Line, Darkdeserthighway, Jasmine Affanalis, and others are genuine closers who will be shuffled into midfield positions against their will, with Tanzanite Diamond and Bella Colombia the most likely to actually secure the rear berths given their handlers' typical instructions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Werifesteria and Sonic Invader push each other along and create a strong early gallop that shreds hold-up horses' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo off two fighting leaders sets up a race for the horse travelling smoothly in third or fourth, able to pounce entering the straight without having expended energy fighting for position; the Good to Firm surface rewards a horse with a clean stride that can sustain its run over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Sonic Invader under Colin Keane — gets a soft enough early lead when the other fails to press, allowing a controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: A single uncontested leader sets a fair but manageable pace and the horse who leads has enough left in the tank to hold on as the closers fail to close fully in the straight; Good to Firm ground rewards the horse on the front end who doesn't have to dig deep until the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Swoop Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel burns both leaders out before the turn and a horse settled in the first half of the field delivers a well-timed run into the straight.
scenarios.body: A fast early fraction uses up Werifesteria and Sonic Invader, leaving the race wide open for horses who have travelled kindly in the first half of the field and can find a clear run; this suits horses with proven form on Good to Firm and some tactical versatility at a mile-plus.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce enough to collapse the race and a hold-up horse manages to navigate traffic in a 25-runner field.
scenarios.body: This is structurally the hardest scenario to land given how many genuine closers are squeezed into midfield against their natural style, reducing the chance any of them achieve the ideal late position; the redistribution of so many hold-up types into midfield means a pure late closer finding clear daylight in a big field is the least reliable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sonic Invader vs Werifesteria duel — watch which of the two secures the lead cleanly at the start; if one capitulates early the other instantly becomes the race-shaper and their chance transforms from front-runner to potential winner.

races.name: Fegentri World Championship (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: Progressive profile over big trips on good ground, finishing second over 18f and winning over 14f in similar conditions; the 7lb claimer S Langhard rides at 170lbs and 29 days between runs is fine — the strong contested pace is precisely what suits this hold-prominent type trained by De Bromhead.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose sim-going record (8/15) is modest and whose best recent effort was a third over 14f on good ground; Mr Cian Murphy takes a 7lb claim, but the horse's record suggests this longer trip taxes him beyond his comfort zone and a truly-run race may find him out in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has won over 16f on standard going; 40 days off the track and a modest sim-going record (6/12 with no wins) temper expectations, though the step back to turf from all-weather form is potentially helpful — class of a 74 OR marks him as competitive if the race falls right.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over 23f on good ground and back-to-back placed efforts at 14-15f, making the 1m7f trip eminently suitable; only 17 days since last run keeps freshness intact, and the 72 OR gives her weight to carry at 166lbs — she will set the fractions and is the chief pace-influence in this race.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-piece and a hood, has been consistently placed without winning over 11-13f on good ground, and his sim-going record (11/15, no wins, one place) makes him a tough sell at this longer trip; 21 days is a fine gap but the 65 OR and low weight of 159lbs reflect a horse who may find this distance stretching him.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner who carries a clear warning flag for fading in finishes — a critical flaw at 1m7f on good-to-firm; she wears a tongue-tie, is only 14 days off her last run, and her history (9/17f good, 13/13f) paints a picture of a mare who gets competitive early but runs out of fuel, making her a race-shaper rather than a winner here.

runners_data.name: Peace Walk
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by profile whose true style means he will want to race deep and late — mapped to midfield here because the field is overcrowded with hold-up types, so he is likely racing partially out of role; 57 days since last run is the longest break in this field, and his sim-going record of 0 wins from 11 qualifying runs is a red flag at this level.

runners_data.name: Makaiah
runners_data.note: Wears no headgear, trained by Gerard O'Leary whose stable is 1/13 over 14 days, and showed a second place over 12f on good ground in recent form; 45 days since last run may mean a sharpener is needed, but at OR 61 carrying 155lbs he is lightly enough treated to be competitive if the pace scenario sets up for a prominent racer.

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Has a genuine win over 17f on good going on his cv and a further third over 16f, making the distance profile encouraging; tagged as fading late and displaced from his preferred hold-up berth by the overcrowded rear, his STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers confidence, but raw form credentials here are among the most relevant in the field — he just needs room to close.

runners_data.name: Supreme Law
runners_data.note: 364 days off the track makes this an enormous absence question mark — effectively a seasonal debut; sim-going record is 0 wins from 15 qualifying runs, all in soft or heavier conditions where the 0/0 win-place record reflects a horse well below this class of form, and the fades-in-finish flag combined with redistribution from hold-up makes this the most speculative runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Catalani and Miss Gitana are the two confirmed front-runners in a field of ten over this extended 1m7f trip on good-to-firm ground at Leopardstown, and their presence together guarantees a contested early pace rather than a dawdle. Catalani has strong good-ground form and has won over marathon trips before, while Miss Gitana carries a notable tendency to fade in the finish — meaning she is likely to cut her own throat if she tries to dominate unchallenged. The honest gallop that results from their duel should ensure the race is truly run, gradually stringing out the field and steadily draining the finish from any horse that over-commits through the middle sectors. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-midfield horse with proven stamina on good-to-firm ground who can sit just off the pace, avoid the early war, and pick up the pieces when the front two tie each other up in the closing stages. Peace Walk, He Who Dares, and Supreme Law are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; of the three, He Who Dares and Peace Walk are the most likely to secure a workable position given their slightly higher ORs and more recent racecourse appearances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Catalani and Miss Gitana fight it out up front and a prominent tracker sits close enough to pounce.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other off over the long Leopardstown straight, leaving them vulnerable to a horse that tracked at close quarters without expending energy in the duel; the stamina test on good-to-firm ground rewards those who have already proven themselves over this kind of trip in this going. Chutzpal, with two wins over similar distances in good conditions and solid recent form, is ideally placed to exploit this shape, while Makaiah showed a placed effort at 12f on good ground and could figure here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Gitana drops away early and Catalani is left to control a moderate, uncontested gallop.
scenarios.body: With one true front-runner suddenly in full command, the pace becomes controlled rather than punishing, and Catalani's class relative to this handicap mark and good-ground form over comparable trips comes into its own. A lone leader who sets their own fractions at 1m7f on a flat track in this going can simply outstay rivals who were never able to get close enough to challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, creating a true staying test that rewards the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Despite redistribution overcrowding the midfield, He Who Dares has a course-and-distance win on similar going to his name and, if able to find any clear run in the final two furlongs, possesses the profile to finish fastest of all; Peace Walk also has a distant form angle at this sort of trip, though both horses are compromised by racing out of their preferred role. The scenario only fully materialises if the pace is red-hot and the prominent horses are all used up, leaving clear daylight for late finishers — a lower-probability outcome given the redistribution caveats.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse, Any Can Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is ragged or the field bunches mid-race and the race degenerates into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a muddling, slowly-run renewal, the better-handicapped, lower-weighted horses get a flat-track speed chance they wouldn't normally have, and a horse like Not Just Any Eagle or Boxing Great, both capable of producing a one-off effort when conditions neutralise their stamina limitations, might benefit. This is the least likely outcome given two genuine front-runners entered, but the presence of amateur jockeys throughout means tactical errors cannot be completely ruled out.

watchPoints.text: Miss Gitana fades in the finish — watch whether she surrenders the lead before the two-furlong pole and hands the race to any horse that tracked her patiently from second or third.

Catalani's ability to dictate alone if Miss Gitana drops away early is the pivotal race shape factor — a solo front-runner at 1m7f on good-to-firm could simply steal the race if the field allows her a soft lead.

He Who Dares and Peace Walk are both true hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by redistribution — watch whether Mr J C Barry and Miss N Lockhead Anderson can find clear running in the straight, because if traffic is a problem the scenario they would win collapses entirely.

Chutzpal's jockey S Langhard is a 5lb claimer — watch whether the prominent position can be controlled through the middle portion of the race, as any positional mistakes at this trip on a flat track are very difficult to recover from.

Supreme Law returns after 364 days off — watch early in the race whether the horse settles and travels, as any signs of rustiness or laboured movement should be noted before drawing any conclusions about form at the subsequent run.
